bridge_strengths: Transition from delegation to continuing judgment (C19.7) is clearly stated and supported by user activities in C19.8–C19.9.
Shift from judgment to task understanding (C19.10) logically interprets the cited activities as requiring situation awareness.
Link between task understanding and situation-awareness literature (C19.11) is explicit and justified by prior research.
Evidence for the value of situation awareness (C19.12–C19.13) and subjective situation awareness (C19.14) is correctly sourced and supports the argument.
Return to programming agents (C19.17) closes the loop, showing why CASA is a meaningful research problem.
response.overall_assessment: The second paragraph builds a coherent chain from delegation to the research problem. All transitions are logically sound and well-supported by the cited evidence, which is accurately used according to the evidence audit. No revisions are required.

supported_claims: Kumar et al. (2025) correctly cited to show incremental interaction and adjustment lead to task success.
Dhanorkar et al. (2026) correctly cited to show developers continuously judge progress at various stages.
Jaeger and Eckhardt (2021) correctly cited to show situational information security awareness influences perceived threat, coping, and actual security behavior.
Nadj et al. (2020) correctly cited to show system performance improvement may not increase user situation awareness.
Rose et al. (2018) correctly cited to show task-specific subjective situation awareness can predict objective and subjective performance and is distinct from workload.
Endsley (2023) correctly cited as a general reference for the importance of situation awareness in human-AI interaction.
response.overall_assessment: The paragraph appropriately uses evidence from adjacent dynamic-task settings to motivate the study of CASA without claiming that subjective situation awareness in coding agents has already been shown to cause performance, control, satisfaction, or behavior. All cited works are accurately characterized, and the conclusion that CASA constitutes a worthwhile research question is properly derived from the presented evidence.
